newsitem.title: UK: French strikes rattle European gasoline market.
newsitem.headline: French strikes rattle European gasoline market.

text.p: A 10-day-old blockade by striking French truckers and a 24-hour work stoppage at three Elf Aquitaine refineries rattled the European gasoline market on Wednesday, traders and analysts said.
Gasoline exports out of France were expected to temporarily jump after 218 barricades were held on roads and petrol stations and at 12 of 13 refineries, leading to fuel rationing, they said.
"On the mogas front this means that they will export more...because of a halt on local demand," said a trader at an Italian refinery.

France exported 3.6 million tonnes of gasoline in 1995, or about 84,000 barrels per day (bpd), mostly to Germany, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, the former Soviet Union and Iran, according to data from the International Energy Agency.
But the industrial action could tighten supplies in Europe, particularly in the Med, if refinery production was affected through the weekend, they said.

"If it goes through the weekend then what we would expect to see is some impact on European prices given the level of French exports to neighbouring countries," said Peter Bogin, associate director of Cambridge Energy Research Associates in Paris.
"I would have to assume that with 10 percent of the gasoline stations closed in France that demand has dropped off because people aren't filling up their tanks," he said.
Royal Dutch/Shell Group said on Wednesday it plans to cut production by 20 to 30 percent at its Berre refinery in southern France from Thursday if a blockade is not resolved.
The plan was drawn up mainly because of problems getting deliveries into the 127,000 barrel per day refinery, rather than a problem of storing unsold products.
Storage tanks at the plant were relatively empty following a maintenance shutdown last month.
Total SA said it had no problems keeping its French refineries running at capacity at least until the weekend.

Meanwhile, distribution workers protesting a planned 10 percent cut in staff at Elf subsidiary Elf Antar were to stage strikes at the 98,000 bpd Grandpuits refinery near Paris, at the 128,000 bpd Feyzin refinery near Lyon and at the 214,000 bpd Donges refinery in western France.
"If it finishes before the weekend you're going to have pretty full tanks at French refineries and you could have a negative impact on prices," Bogin said.
"If it goes beyond the weekend...it will cause a one-time surge in demand," he said. "The longer term effects will be nil."
Truckers and bosses made progress on key demands in marathon negotiations on Wednesday but unions kept up the blockade.
In the second quarter domestic consumption fell 4.2 percent versus a year ago to 360,000 barrels per day, and in July fell 2.0 percent to 390,000 bpd, the IEA said.
Traders said Med prices were hurt slightly by the French strike, but the market was so weak compared to the U.S. that the arbitrage was open and supplies were being shipped across the Atlantic.
